parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module wires one concern, couriers, but it breaks its own in-port/out-port abstraction in how it binds CreateCurierInPort. (1) CreateCurierInPort is registered twice. The first provider builds a CreateCurierInteractor through useFactory. The second binds the same token to CurierRepository with useClass. The binding for one token lives in two conflicting places, and in NestJS the later provider wins. So the controller would get the repository instead of the use case, and the interactor is never used. (2) The CreateCurierInteractor factory injects CreateCurierInPort, its own in-port, instead of CreateCurierOutPort. CreateCurierOutPort is registered as a provider bound to CurierRepository, but nothing injects it. This sidesteps the ports pattern the module uses everywhere else: every other interactor takes out-ports such as FindCurierByIdWithOrdersOutPort and SaveCurierOutPort. (3) FindCountOfFreeCuriersOutPort is also registered without being injected anywhere, which adds to the inconsistent wiring. Because of the duplicated binding and the bypassed abstraction, the unit fails the rubric.
